scope: First direct fixed-optimum paleoTS/joint-OU practice wave; not denominator-complete.
queries: paleoTS alpha half-life adaptation fossil time series Ornstein-Uhlenbeck
paleoTS half-life alpha Nature Communications evolution

direct_empirical_targets.citation: Hunt G, Bell MA, Travis MP. 2008. Evolution toward a new adaptive optimum: phenotypic evolution in a fossil stickleback lineage. Evolution 62:700-710.
direct_empirical_targets.evidence: The paper fits the joint multivariate-normal fixed-optimum OU model later bundled in paleoTS, defines alpha as strength of the restraining force around the optimum, translates alpha into stabilizing-selection quantities, and reports half-lives of 853, 580 and 635 generations for three traits.
direct_empirical_targets.independent_biological_evidence: yes; morphology, population-genetic plausibility checks and adaptive-landscape interpretation are discussed

direct_empirical_targets.citation: Lo Cascio Saetre C et al. 2017. Rapid adaptive phenotypic change following colonization of a newly restored habitat. Nature Communications 8:14159.
direct_empirical_targets.system: 19-year reed-warbler body-mass time series after habitat colonization
direct_empirical_targets.evidence: The article reports alpha=0.39 as the strength of the restraining force around the optimum, converts it to half-life 1.76 years, and interprets the result as very rapid adaptation. It also reports ecological, fitness and genetic evidence supporting adaptation.
direct_empirical_targets.independent_biological_evidence: yes; survival-body-mass association, fitness variation and genetic/ecological evidence

methodological_context.citation: Voje KL. 2023. Fitting and evaluating univariate and multivariate models of within-lineage evolution. Paleobiology.
methodological_context.note: Describes paleoTS fixed-OU as trait pull toward an adaptive optimum at rate alpha and half-life as the time to move halfway to the optimum; also develops reciprocal multivariate OU and Granger-causal models, which are conceded as prior art rather than counted as the present novelty.
Documents alpha as strength of attraction to the optimum and states that in a microevolutionary context the parameters can be related to natural selection and genetic drift.

interpretation: The fixed-optimum corollary targets a real empirical practice in at least two independent systems, including a Nature Communications field time series. This wave establishes non-vacuous practice relevance but not prevalence. Both examples also contain external biological evidence, so the theorem qualifies what the trait likelihood alone identifies; it does not negate their broader adaptive arguments.
hard_stop: Do not report 2/2 as a field prevalence estimate; this is a seed/wave audit, not a denominator-complete systematic review.
